note: Redesigned per the follow-up IA request: 'primary' is a flat 5-item main menu — Home, About, Programs, Impact, Contact — matching the 5 pages the client named. 'About', 'Programs' and 'Impact' each carry a dropdown/submenu child ('About' > 'Partnerships'; 'Programs' > 'Register / Apply'; 'Impact' > 'News & events') for content judged too distinct to fold further into its parent page as a plain section without bloating it or mixing dissimilar update cadences (News & events churns weekly; Impact & sustainability is a mostly-static annual narrative) — everything else from the original 21-page inventory is already an in-page anchored subsection (see pages/_index.json's note). None of 'Partnerships', 'Apply' or 'News & events' is a top-level nav item; each is reached only via its parent's dropdown, plus section-level links in the matching footer column. 'Contact' moved from footer-only to a full primary nav item. The template's client-side router used '#/<page>' hash routes for all of the 'page' values above; content-seeding-plan.md recommends converting these to real WordPress page slugs/URLs (the mapping from page-key to final slug lives in pages/_index.json's 'slug' field). Values containing '#' (e.g. 'about#consortium', 'programs#register') point to an anchored subsection within that page's merged content, not a separate page.
